MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted name] Medical Center
Department of Clinical Genetics

Patient: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted]
MRN: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Peripheral Blood
Date Collected: [redacted]
Date Received: [redacted]
Date Reported: [redacted]

REFERRAL REASON
Diagnostic testing for genetic susceptibility to breast/ovarian cancer.

TEST PERFORMED
BRCA1 and BRCA2 Comprehensive Analysis
- Bidirectional DNA sequencing of BRCA1 and BRCA2 exons
- MLPA (Multiplex Ligation-dependent Probe Amplification) dosage analysis
- Previous protein truncation test (PTT) for nonsense mutations in BRCA1 exon 11 and BRCA2 exons 10-11

METHODOLOGY
DNA was extracted from peripheral blood lymphocytes. Initial screening was performed using protein truncation testing (PTT) for BRCA1 exon 11 and BRCA2 exons 10-11 to detect nonsense mutations. Current analysis included unidirectional fluorescent DNA sequencing of the remaining exons:
- BRCA1: Exons 2-3, 5-10, 12-24 including intron-exon boundaries
- BRCA2: Exons 2-9, 12-27 including intron-exon boundaries

All splice sites were analyzed with a minimum of 20 base pairs of intronic sequence. MLPA analysis was performed using the MRC-Holland P002 and P045 probe sets to detect large deletions and duplications in BRCA1 and BRCA2.

Analytical sensitivity: >98% for detection of point mutations and small insertions/deletions in the regions analyzed.

RESULTS

BRCA1 (NM_007294.3): No pathogenic variants detected
- Sequencing: No point mutations identified
- MLPA: No deletions or duplications detected

BRCA2 (NM_000059.3): No pathogenic variants detected
- Sequencing: No point mutations identified
- MLPA: No deletions or duplications detected

SUMMARY
Comprehensive analysis of BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes revealed no pathogenic variants. No deletions or duplications were detected by MLPA dosage analysis. No point mutations were identified in either gene through bidirectional sequencing and protein truncation testing.

Based on these results, the patient is very unlikely to have a BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation. This significantly reduces but does not eliminate the possibility of hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome.

LIMITATIONS
This test has a clinical sensitivity of >98% for detecting point mutations and small insertions/deletions. Large genomic rearrangements outside the regions covered by MLPA probes, deep intronic variants, and regulatory region variants are not detected by this analysis. Variants in other genes associated with hereditary cancer syndromes were not evaluated.
